slides.3.title: Lisboa: The Nine Sub-DOCs
slides.3.html:
The Lisboa wine region is Portugal's most diverse, containing nine sub-DOCs that stretch from north of Lisbon to the lower Tagus.

🗺️ The nine sub-DOCs

Sub-DOC Character Main varieties
Arruda Limestone hills, maritime climate Fernão Pires, Aragonez
Alenquer North of Lisbon, varied soils, quality leap in recent years Castelão, Touriga Nacional
Torres Vedras Traditional high-volume area, shifting towards quality Touriga Nacional, Vital
Óbidos Limestone, Atlantic influence, aromatic whites Arinto, Fernão Pires
Lourinhã Famous for brandy (Aguardente) Malvasia Rei (brandy grape)
Encostas d'Aire Limestone, higher altitude, fresh whites Fernão Pires, Arinto
Bucelas ⭐ Home of high-acid Arinto whites, historic appellation Arinto (at least 75%)
Colares ⭐ Dune sand, ungrafted Ramisco, rare in the world Ramisco (red), Malvasia (white)
Carcavelos Near-extinct off-dry fortified DOC Galego Dourado and other rare varieties
slides.4.title: Lisboa: Coastal vs. Inland Styles
slides.4.items.0.label: Coastal areas (Colares / Bucelas)
slides.4.items.0.desc: Cool Atlantic winds, sand or limestone, fresh and high in acidity, light and mineral; the heartland of Arinto and Ramisco
slides.4.items.1.label: Inland hills (Alenquer / Arruda)
slides.4.items.1.desc: Further from the sea and warmer in summer, with red limestone-clay soils producing fuller-bodied reds, mainly Touriga Nacional and Castelão
slides.4.items.2.label: Traditional high-volume area (Torres Vedras)
slides.4.items.2.desc: Historically known for large volumes of cheap wine, now shifting towards quality; the introduction of Touriga Nacional is lifting quality
slides.4.items.3.label: Special styles (Carcavelos / Lourinhã)
slides.4.items.3.desc: Fortified sweet wine (Carcavelos) and brandy (Lourinhã), unique treasures within Lisboa
slides.5.question: How many sub-DOCs does the Lisboa region have?
slides.5.explanation: The Lisboa region has nine sub-DOCs: Arruda・Alenquer・Torres Vedras・Óbidos・Lourinhã・Encostas d'Aire・Bucelas・Colares・Carcavelos, each with its own soils, climate and main varieties.
slides.6.question: Which Lisboa sub-DOC is famous for ungrafted old-vine Ramisco on dune soils, a living fossil of the wine world?
slides.6.explanation: Colares is one of the rarest wine regions in the world. Its vines grow in Atlantic coastal dunes, with roots going straight into deep sand. Because sand protects against phylloxera, Colares's Ramisco vines have never needed grafting, making it one of the few regions with substantial areas of ungrafted old vines.
